chunks: Al-Khazzaz, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) on the Day of Judgment will hold onto the waist-knot of Allah, and we will hold onto the waist-knot of our Prophet, and our Shia will hold onto our waist-knot. Then he said: The waist-knot means light.

key_terms.النُّورُ: The light, defining the metaphorical meaning of the waist-knot
key_terms.حُجْزَة: Waist-knot or girdle, used metaphorically for a spiritual connection or link of authority

ai.seo_question: What does 'hujzah' (waist-knot) mean in the context of the Day of Judgment according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) describes a metaphysical hierarchy of spiritual attachment on the Day of Judgment, where the Prophet holds onto Allah's 'hujzah' (waist-knot), the Imams hold the Prophet's, and the faithful hold the Imams'. The explicit definition of 'hujzah' as 'light' (nur) in this narration underscores the Shia doctrine of spiritual intercession and the luminous nature of divine proximity, distinguishing it from physical grasping. This concept reinforces the theological principle that salvation is achieved through adherence to the Ahl al-Bayt, who serve as the luminous conduits of divine grace.

en.ammaar-muslim: 5. [5/333] al-Tawhid and al-Uyun: My father from Sa’d from Ibn Isa from al-Hasan b. Ali al-Khazzaz from Abi al-Hasan al-Ridha عليه السلام who said:

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه واله will hold on to the waist-knot of Allah on the Day of Judgment, we will hold on to the waist-knot of our prophet, and our Shia (followers) will hold on to our waist-knot. Then he said: waist-knot means light.
